entries.summary: Code review of ION-16397 booking-cargoscreen AWS SDK v1→2.x migration: 3 substantive findings from bytecode verification
entries.detail:
Branch feature/ION-16397-bk-cargoscreen-aws-upgrade, single commit 2f8a4829e8, 19 files.

FINDING 1 (High) - AbortedException catch is now dead code.
javap on cloud-sdk-aws SqsMessagingClient shows every method (incl. receiveMessages) funnels failures through
private handleException(...) which ALWAYS returns MessagingException (extends RuntimeException) and rethrows.
v1 commons SQSClient.receiveMessage had NO try/catch, so com.amazonaws.AbortedException propagated to
SqsMessageHandler.start() -> stop() + Thread.interrupt(). Now software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.AbortedException
is wrapped in MessagingException, so `catch (AbortedException)` at SqsMessageHandler.java:78 can never fire.
Interrupt during long-poll falls to `catch (Exception)` -> log + `while (notStopped)` retries immediately -> hot
error loop. Fix: catch MessagingException/Exception and unwrap the cause chain for AbortedException/InterruptedException.

FINDING 2 (High) - SQS/SNS client tuning silently dropped; v1 reader/writer split collapsed.
v1 commons SQSModule held TWO AmazonSQS instances (amazonSQSReader + amazonSQSWriter) configured from
com.inttra.mercury.util.AWSConstants:
  STANDARD_SQS_READER_CONFIGURATION  = maxErrorRetry 3, RetryPolicy(fullJitter 500/5000, 3, false),
                                       connTimeout 1000ms, maxConnections 50  (no socketTimeout, no execTimeout)
  STANDARD_SQS_WRITER_CONFIGURATION  = maxErrorRetry 3, same policy, connTimeout 1000ms,
                                       clientExecutionTimeout 10000ms, socketTimeout 5000ms, maxConnections 50
  STANDARD_SNS_PUBLISH_CONFIGURATION = maxErrorRetry 2, same policy, connTimeout 1000ms,
                                       clientExecutionTimeout 10000ms, socketTimeout 5000ms, maxConnections 50
Replacement MessagingClientFactory.createDefaultStringClient() / NotificationClientFactory.createDefaultClient(arn)
both use DefaultRetryStrategy.standardStrategyBuilder().build() (2 retries, standard retryable predicate, circuit
breaker ON) + ApacheHttpClient(maxConnections 50, connTimeout 5000ms, socketTimeout 30s, connAcqTimeout 10s),
region pinned US_EAST_1, and NO apiCallTimeout. So: retries 3->2 on SQS and 2->2 on SNS but with a *different*
predicate (403/404 no longer retried), connect 1s->5s, DLQ-send socket 5s->30s, exec deadline 10s->none, and one
shared client for long-poll receive + delete + DLQ send. ION-16380 (watermill) explicitly kept the reader/writer
split and asserted distinctness. Asymmetry: S3 tuning preserved to the byte, SQS/SNS silently defaulted. Neither
the design doc nor the commit message mentions this.

FINDING 3 (Medium) - S3ClientTuningTest asserts the ingredients, not the wiring.
backoffIsFullJitterExponentialCappedAt5000ms builds its own BackoffStrategy.exponentialDelay(...) instead of
reading it off s3RetryStrategy(); retryPredicateRetriesEvenNonRetryableExceptions calls s3RetryPredicate()
directly. Swapping exponentialDelayWithoutJitter, or dropping .retryOnException(...)/.throttlingBackoffStrategy(...)
/.circuitBreakerEnabled(false) inside s3RetryStrategy(), would not fail any test. Only maxAttempts() and
useClientDefaults() are read back off the real strategy.

Also noted: no production call site sets DO_NOT_DELETE / DO_NO_SEND_TO_DLQ (grep: only tests), so the adapter
guards a mechanism production never activates today - correct to preserve, but the risk framing was theoretical.
S3 region hard-coded us-east-1 in Java while ES region comes from YAML (esConfiguration.region) - three different
region-resolution mechanisms now. MessagingClient is AutoCloseable and never closed at shutdown.
cloud-sdk 1.0.28-SNAPSHOT has advanced (20260724 -> 20260805) since the branch was built; re-verify.

entries.summary: Review fixes implemented: F1 abort handling, F2(c) reader/writer split, F3 mutation-verified tests, F4 S3 region config. F5 withdrawn as my error.
entries.detail:
F5 CORRECTION - I was wrong, user was right.
  commons source of truth = mercury-services-commons branch feature/ION-12310-commons-cloudsdk-refactoring (HEAD 1293c50):
    cloud-sdk-api/.../messaging/api/MessagingClient.java:14  -> "public interface MessagingClient<T> {"  (NOT AutoCloseable)
    cloud-sdk-aws/.../messaging/aws/impl/SqsMessagingClient.java:53 -> no close() method at all
  Cached jars DISAGREE with each other:
    cloud-sdk-api-1.0.28-20260724.194357-1.jar -> not AutoCloseable
    cloud-sdk-api-1.0.28-20260805.053457-2.jar -> extends AutoCloseable   <-- what -SNAPSHOT.jar resolves to
  So the published SNAPSHOT contains API absent from the source branch => build-integrity hazard for every module.
  environment.lifecycle().manage(...) code was written then REVERTED; a comment in bindSqsReaderClient() records why.
  My original F5 also claimed StorageClient was closeable - simply wrong, it has no close() in any build.

IMPLEMENTED (all on feature/ION-16397-bk-cargoscreen-aws-upgrade, NOT committed, NOT pushed):
 F1 SqsMessageHandler.start(): single catch(Exception) + static isAbortSignal(Throwable) walking the cause chain for
    AbortedException/InterruptedException, self-reference guard, Thread.isInterrupted() fallback. 6 tests.
 F2(c) Reader/writer SQS split restored: BookingCargoScreenApplicationInjector.SQS_READER / SQS_WRITER @Named
    @Singleton providers; SqsMessageHandler ctor now (reader, writer, sqsConfig, threadPoolConfig, task); receives on
    reader, deleteMessage + DLQ sendMessage on writer; CargoScreenEventProcessor injects both by @Named.
    Tests: listenerAndSenderGetSeparateMessagingClients, receivesUseTheReaderAndWritesUseTheWriter.
    NOTE: the SQS/SNS retry+timeout tuning delta is STILL OPEN - user decision pending.
 F3 4 behavioural tests driving the built strategy via acquireInitialToken/refreshRetryToken. VERIFIED BY MUTATION:
      exponentialDelay->exponentialDelayWithoutJitter  => theInstalledBackoffIsJitteredAndCapped
      circuitBreakerEnabled(false)->(true)             => theInstalledStrategyHasNoCircuitBreaker
      .retryOnException(...) deleted                   => theInstalledPredicateRetriesNonRetryableExceptions (+3)
      maxAttempts(4)->6                                => theInstalledStrategyStopsAfterThreeRetries (+2)
    throttlingBackoffStrategy still unasserted (cannot synthesise a throttling response through this API).
 F4 New S3Config {region, DEFAULT_REGION="us-east-1"}; BookingCargoScreenApplicationConfig.s3Config initialised to a
    default instance so the YAML block is optional; s3StorageConfig() -> s3StorageConfig(String region);
    s3Config.region added explicitly to conf/{int,qa,cvt,prod}/config.yaml. This ENDS the "zero config change" claim.
    SQS/SNS regions remain pinned inside cloud-sdk factories - not overridable via createDefault*Client().

BUILD: 69 -> 84 tests. Full `clean verify` BUILD SUCCESS observed twice with these changes.
FLAKY (pre-existing, timing/load dependent, NOT caused by these changes - same code passed green twice):
  BoundedThreadPoolTest, CargoScreenProcessorManagedHandlerTest, SqsMessageHandlerTest.testWebApplicationError
  (the last one's own source comment admits "This could be a brittle test"). Worth stabilising separately.

entries.summary: Retry predicate switched to v2 standard for ALL clients; SQS/SNS v1 tuning carried over; 82 tests green; INT boot clean HTTP 200
entries.detail:
USER DECISION: use the AWS SDK v2 standard retry predicate uniformly, including S3 ("makes no sense to retry 403/404").
Then: also carry SQS/SNS tuning parity as far as the libraries permit, all tests green, app boots clean.

CRITICAL GOTCHA FOUND: StandardRetryStrategy.builder() and DefaultRetryStrategy.standardStrategyBuilder() do NOT
carry the standard retry predicates on the returned object. They are merged in by the AWS client builder at build
time, and ONLY when useClientDefaults()==true. The previous code had useClientDefaults(false) + retryOnException(
alwaysTrue) to reproduce v1. Simply deleting retryOnException from that yields a strategy that retries NOTHING.
Verified empirically: refreshRetryToken threw "Request attempt 1 encountered non-retryable failure" even for
RetryableException. => must use DefaultRetryStrategy.standardStrategyBuilder() and leave useClientDefaults true.
Consequence: retryability CANNOT be asserted on the bare strategy object in a unit test. The load-bearing assertion
is useClientDefaults()==true. SdkDefaultRetryStrategy (which does carry the predicates) is in
software.amazon.awssdk.core.INTERNAL.retry - deliberately not used in production code.

FINAL SHAPE (BookingCargoScreenApplicationInjector):
  retryStrategy(int maxAttempts) - shared: standardStrategyBuilder + maxAttempts + fullJitter(500,5000) as both
      backoffStrategy and throttlingBackoffStrategy + circuitBreakerEnabled(false). Used by all 4 clients.
  httpClient(Duration socketTimeout) - shared: connect 1000ms, maxConnections 50, per-client socket timeout.
  v1 values carried (from AWSConstants decompilation):
      S3          attempts 4, socket 5000ms,  execTimeout 60s (v1 had none; cloud-sdk forces one, 39s worst case)
      SQS reader  attempts 4, socket 50s,     execTimeout 240s (v1 set NEITHER; 50s is v1's SDK default and MUST
                  exceed the 10s long poll - do not copy the writer's 5s)
      SQS writer  attempts 4, socket 5000ms,  execTimeout 10000ms  (v1 really did set 10s)
      SNS         attempts 3, socket 5000ms,  execTimeout 10000ms  (v1 withMaxErrorRetry(2) - one fewer!)
  AwsMessagingClientConfig validates queueUrl non-empty AND maxMessages 1..10 -> sqsClientConfig takes the whole
  SQSConfig so the client defaults come from the same config the handler uses.
  S3Config renamed -> AwsConfig (it now supplies the region for S3, SQS and SNS); YAML key s3Config -> awsConfig.

TESTS: S3ClientTuningTest replaced by AwsClientTuningTest (13 tests) covering all four client configs.
  82 tests total, 0 failures, exit 0.
BOOT: mvn package + java -jar ... server conf/int/config.yaml with `aws configure export-credentials` env vars.
  "Building AWS clients for region us-east-1", S3StorageClient resolved creds, JestModule connected to INT ES,
  Jetty 8080/8081 up, GET /admin/healthcheck -> HTTP 200 all healthy, ZERO ERROR lines in 40 log lines.
  startListeners resolves Set<Processor> which requires both @Named SQS clients + the SNS publisher, so all four
  clients were really constructed against INT settings; ~35s of live polling with no errors also validates the
  reader's 50s socket timeout against the 10s long poll.
  Only pre-existing warnings remain (Log4j2 StatusLogger, Jersey provider, logback 1.5.32 vs 1.5.33).

entries.summary: Region now from DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain (zero config changes); AWS event POJOs replaced with local ones -> zero com.amazonaws imports; 86 tests green
entries.detail:
USER PUSHBACK, both correct:
 (a) remove the region config and use AWS defaults
 (b) why import AWS v1 S3 libraries just for JSON deserialisation

CHANGE 1 - region from the default provider chain.
  cloud-sdk S3ClientFactory / MessagingClientFactory.createConfiguredClient /
  NotificationClientFactory.createConfiguredClient all call config.getRegion().getRegionDelegate() unconditionally,
  and BaseAwsConfig.validateBaseConfig rejects null ("Region must not be null"). AWS SDK v1 had no such requirement -
  it used DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain. Fix: resolve the chain in the injector and pass the result.
    String region() { configured if non-blank, else DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain.builder().build().getRegion().id() }
  AwsConfig.region is now an OPTIONAL override defaulting to null; DEFAULT_REGION constant deleted; the awsConfig
  block was REMOVED from all four config.yaml files -> conf/ is byte-identical to HEAD again (zero config changes).
  Net effect: removes hard-coding rather than adding config (was Region.US_EAST_1 in the injector for S3, and
  MessagingClientFactory.DEFAULT_REGION / NotificationClientFactory.DEFAULT_REGION inside cloud-sdk for SQS/SNS).

CHANGE 2 - local event POJOs, AWS v1 types gone from source.
  KEY FACT: com.amazonaws.services.s3.event.S3EventNotification ships in aws-java-sdk-s3:1.12.730 (AWS SDK v1 S3),
  NOT in aws-lambda-java-events (which only provides S3Event + SNSEvent). The module only needed two strings from
  the payload: bucket name and object key.
  New: processor/model/SnsNotification.java and processor/model/S3EventNotification.java - minimal @Data +
  @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) POJOs parsed by the existing SNSMapper (which enables
  ACCEPT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_PROPERTIES so "Records"/"Message" and lower-case both work, and does NOT disable
  FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES - hence ignoreUnknown is mandatory at every level).
  CRITICAL PARITY DETAIL: v1 S3ObjectEntity.getKey() is a plain field return (NO url decoding);
  getUrlDecodedKey() is the decoding one and the module never used it. So the POJO returns the raw percent-encoded
  key - asserted by theObjectKeyIsNotUrlDecoded.
  aws-lambda-java-events dependency REMOVED from pom; confirmed gone from the shaded jar.
  RESULT: grep '^import com.amazonaws' over src/main AND src/test -> ZERO matches.

New test: processor/model/S3EventNotificationParsingTest (4 tests) - real AWS SNS+S3 envelope end-to-end, case
  sensitivity both ways, raw key preservation, unknown fields at every level. No mocking.

BUILD: 86 tests, 0 failures, BUILD SUCCESS.
BOOT: could NOT be re-run - the local SSO token expired at 23:00 ("Token has expired and refresh failed"), so
  `aws sts get-caller-identity` and `aws configure export-credentials` both fail. The boot attempt died in
  ParameterStoreConfigTransform -> SsmCloudParameterStore.getParameter during CONFIG PARSING, before Guice is built
  and therefore before region() is ever called - i.e. environmental, not caused by these changes. Region resolution
  is covered instead by the unit test regionResolvesFromTheDefaultProviderChainWhenNotConfigured, which passed with
  no awsConfig block and AWS_REGION unset. Re-run the boot after `aws sso login`.

STILL TRUE: aws-java-sdk-core/kms/s3/sns/sqs remain in the shaded jar via cloud-sdk-aws, and aws-java-sdk-core is
  LOAD-BEARING for Elasticsearch SigV4 signing (cloudsdk.aws.module.JestModule uses v1
  DefaultAWSCredentialsProviderChain + vc.inreach.aws.request.AWSSigner).
